vo.text: Imagine the quietest place you have ever been.
Now make it quieter.
High on a mountain, outside the city of Makkah, there is a small cave.
It is only a few steps long. Just enough room to sit, and to pray.
The mountain is called Jabal an-Noor. The Mountain of Light. And the cave is called Heera.
Down in the valley, life was loud.
People bowed to statues made of stone and wood. The strong pushed the weak aside, and almost no one asked why.
But one man used to climb up here, alone, for many nights at a time.
He was forty years old. His name was Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
Everyone in Makkah knew one thing about him. He never lied. They called him al-Ameen. The one you can trust.
He brought a little food and water, and he stayed to think, to worship Allah, and to wait.
Then, one night in the month of Ramadan, he was not alone in the cave anymore.
An angel had come. The angel Jibreel, sent by Allah.
And the angel said one word. Ikra. Read.
Muhammad could not read or write. So he answered: I am not one who reads.
The angel held him close, so tightly he could hardly bear it, then let him go, and said again: Read.
Three times the angel asked. Three times he gave the same answer.
And then the angel recited the very first words of the Qur'an.
Read, in the name of your Lord, who created.
Created the human being from a clinging clot.
Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous,
who taught by the pen,
taught the human being what he did not know.
Think about that. The very first word was not fight, or run, or be afraid.
It was read. Learn. Understand.
Muhammad hurried home, his heart beating fast, to his wife Khadeejah. Cover me, he said. Cover me.
She wrapped him up, and comforted him. Allah will never let you down, she said. You are kind to your family, and you help people in need.
That night was only the beginning. For twenty three years, more words would come down, piece by piece, until the whole Quran was complete.
Tonight, one lantern rises over the mountain. On it, one word. Read.
Tomorrow night. What Khadeejah did next, and the old man who knew what it meant.
